title: Spatially Compact Dense Block Mining in Spatial Tensors

problem.claim: The task is to discover dense blocks in spatial tensors that cover small spatial regions.

gap.claim: Most existing dense block mining algorithms maximize density alone, producing spatially loose blocks that cover large regions.

contributions.claim: The paper formulates top-k Spatially Compact Dense block mining and ranks blocks using a scoring function that considers both density and spatial coverage.
The paper uses a filter-refinement framework that generates high-scoring candidate blocks and then applies a traditional dense block mining algorithm to increase candidate density.
The paper develops top-down and bottom-up filtering solutions that approximately optimize the new scoring function for the NP-hard problem.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Evaluations on four real datasets report comparable density values and significantly smaller spatial coverage than dense blocks returned by existing dense block mining algorithms.

narrative_sequence.summary: Spatial tensors are used in applications including remote sensing, geospatial information systems, conservation planning, and urban planning.
The paper studies mining dense blocks that occupy small spatial regions.
Existing density-focused methods generally produce blocks with overly large spatial coverage.
The proposed approach formulates a joint density-coverage ranking problem and solves it with filter-refinement methods using top-down and bottom-up filtering.
Experiments on four real datasets report similar density and substantially smaller spatial coverage than existing methods.

source_observation.claim: Optimizing density alone can yield dense blocks with large spatial coverage.

interpretation.claim: When compactness matters, the objective should represent both quality and spatial extent.

application.claim: Design ranking or selection functions that jointly score signal strength and the size of the covered region.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that the joint objective is preferable when spatial compactness is not required.

unknowns: The exact scoring function is not specified.
The datasets, parameter settings, baselines, and quantitative results are not described.
Approximation guarantees and computational costs are not reported.
